extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider / runtime:** Azure
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** The deployment targets Azure via GitHub Actions on ubuntu-latest runners, but no region or high-availability configuration is specified in the infrastructure data.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret stores:** GitHub Actions secrets
- **Credential handling:** The Azure credential is referenced as `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` in the IAM principal field, indicating use of GitHub-managed secrets.
- **Assessment:** Secrets are externally stored but not scoped to environments; the same credential appears in both secret store and IAM principal fields, increasing exposure surface.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption at rest:** Not evidenced
- **Key management:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** No encryption or key management configuration is present in the detected infrastructure, leaving data protection status unknown.

### 4) IAM / least privilege
- **Principals / service accounts:** `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` (referenced as managed identity)
- **Scope / permissions / trust:** Subscription-level scope with trust from GitHub Actions; no specific roles or resource-level scoping are defined.
- **Assessment:** The service account has overly broad subscription-level access and lacks resource scoping, violating least-privilege principles.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runners / triggers:** GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners triggered by push and workflow_dispatch
- **OIDC / credential flow:** OIDC is not enabled; credentials are passed via secret reference without short-lived token exchange.
- **Assessment:** Without OIDC, long-lived secrets are exposed to the CI/CD pipeline, increasing credential theft risk.

### 6) Container security
- **Images / root user:** Not evidenced
- **Health checks / resource limits:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** No container configuration is present in the detected infrastructure.

### 7) Top 3 prioritized actions
1. **Implement OIDC for Azure authentication** – Replace `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` with OIDC to eliminate long-lived, cross-pipeline secret exposure.
2. **Scope IAM permissions to specific resource groups** – Change the managed identity scope from subscription to resource-group level, limiting blast radius of a compromised credential.
3. **Define deployment environments** – Add GitHub Environments with secret scoping and approval gates to separate production and non-production credential usage.

relationship_graph_md:
## Component Relationship Graph

- **Entry Points**: The FastAPI framework exposes four API endpoints (`Login`, `Me`, `Logout`, `Chat Endpoint`), all protected by Bearer Auth. No unauthenticated access to any endpoint is shown.

- **Guardrails**: Two guardrails (`Relevance` and `Jailbreak`) sit before agents, both using `gpt-4.1-mini` for classification. They protect the Triage Agent only.

- **Agent Delegation**: The `Triage Agent` delegates to `Flight Status`, `FAQ`, `Cancellation`, and `Seat Booking` agents. All four sub‑agents call the same five unguarded tools (`Baggage`, `Cancel Flight`, `Display Seat Map`, `Faq Lookup`, `Flight Status`).

- **Tool Exposure**: Every agent (including Triage) can reach every tool. Tools like `Cancel Flight` and `Lookup Reservation` have no access controls or audit logs shown. The framework (`OpenAI Agents`) directly calls all tools and all agents—bypassing guardrails.

- **Data Store**: `Sqlite` is declared but has no edges—no agent or tool connects to it, suggesting it is unused or misconfigured.

- **Risk Pattern**: Sub‑agents operate without guardrail coverage, and all tools are unguarded. A jailbroken agent could invoke destructive tools (e.g., `Cancel Flight`) without constraint.
